subject: [PATCH] crash: keep crashkernel CMA pages reserved if activation fails

reviews.author: Bradley Morgan
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch's behavior of marking crashkernel CMA areas as reserved on activation error would also occur under every bitmap_zalloc() failure, and asked if this is accounted for.
reviews.raw_body:
You do know that this will activate under every bitmap_zalloc() failure,
right? Is that accounted for?

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed Bradley Morgan's concern about the crashkernel CMA pages being released when activation fails, explaining that keeping them reserved ensures the first kernel doesn't overwrite or lose data from the vmcore. The author confirmed this is the intended behavior and mentioned an alternative approach in fadump.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, that's intended. By the time cma_activate_area() runs, the range is
already in crashk_cma_ranges[], so the crash kernel will use it no matter
why activation failed. Keeping the pages reserved is the only way to make
sure the first kernel has nothing there that gets overwritten or goes
missing from the vmcore; the area then behaves like a regular
crashkernel= reservation of the same size.

fadump made the same choice; it is what cma_reserve_pages_on_error() was
added for in commit 27d121d0ec6d ("mm/cma: provide option to opt out
from exposing pages on activation failure").

The bitmap is one bit per page (32 KiB per GiB with 4K pages) and is
allocated at core_initcall, so a failure there is very unlikely.

The alternative is to give the memory back and to drop the
range from crashk_cma_ranges[] when activation fails, leaving the crash
kernel with less memory than requested. I do think that is acceptable as
well. But we do need either whats done in this patch or give the memory
back. Happy to send the alternative as v2 is everyone thinks that the
better way forward.

2026-11-04.patch_summary: This patch modifies the crashkernel memory reservation mechanism to keep CMA pages reserved even if their activation fails. This ensures that kernel data written to these pages is not overwritten by the crash kernel and remains available in the dump. The change adds a new function call, cma_reserve_pages_on_error(), which marks the areas as reserved when activation fails.

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Patch was reviewed by Usama and found to be correct. They suggested that losing memory in the first kernel is preferable for debugging purposes.

reviews.author: Bradley Morgan
reviews.summary: Bradley found the patch to be a 'hidden gem' and suggested that it addresses a predicament related to bitmap_zalloc() failure. He applied the Reviewed-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
On 6 November 2026 14:05:54 GMT, Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev> wrote:
>On Fri, 6 Nov 2026 12:21:12 +0100 Mikhail Zaslonko
><zaslonko@linux.ibm.com> wrote:
>
>> 
>> 
>> On 04-Nov-26 15:56, Usama Arif wrote:
>> > reserve_crashkernel_cma() adds each crashkernel CMA area to
>> > crashk_cma_ranges[] as soon as it is declared. If the area later fails
>> > activation, e.g. because movablecore= put the ZONE_MOVABLE boundary
>> > inside it, cma_activate_area() releases the pages to the buddy
>allocator
>> > as ordinary memory. The range is still handed to the crash kernel and
>> > excluded from the vmcore, so kernel data that lands there is
>overwritten
>> > by the crash kernel and missing from the dump.
>> > 
>> > Mark the areas with cma_reserve_pages_on_error(), so that a failed
>> > activation leaves the pages reserved: lost to the first kernel, but
>safe
>> > for the crash kernel to use.
>> > 
>> > Fixes: ab475510e042 ("kdump: implement reserve_crashkernel_cma")
>> > Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
>> > ---
>> s390 hits this without movablecore= (adding the s390 maintainers and
>> linux-s390) since ZONE_DMA ends at 2G here.
>> CMA tries to reserve areas above 4G first, but falls back to lower
>> memory when it doesn't fit, so a cma area can end up across the 2G
>boundary.
>> I ran into this while adding crashkernel=,cma support for s390, which I
>> will post soon, and came up with the same fix.
>> 
>> About dropping the range instead, as you offered for v2: I'd keep this
>> version. With the range dropped, the kdump kernel gets less memory than
>> configured, and that only shows at crash time. With this patch, the
>> the first kernel 'loses' the memory as with a regular crashkernel=
>reservation
>> of the same size.
>
>Yes, I do agree with this. Losing memory in first kernel is preferrable
>and it will then force someone to fix whatever is broken rather than
>finding out when their kernel crashes.
>
>> 
>> There is a second problem in the same loop: all areas are named
>> "crashkernel", which breaks the CMA sysfs and debugfs entries when
>> there are several. I've sent a separate fix for that:
>> 
>>
>https://lore.kernel.org/r/20261106104309.3669583-1-zaslonko@linux.ibm.com
>> 
>
>Thanks! I reviewed this now.
>
>> Reviewed-by: Mikhail Zaslonko <zaslonko@linux.ibm.com>
>> Tested-by: Mikhail Zaslonko <zaslonko@linux.ibm.com>

Well, now that that predicament arises, I see that this patch is a "hidden
gem" sort of thing

Reviewed-by: Bradley Morgan <brads@mainlining.org>

(Thanks for telling me about how you accounted for that bitmap_zalloc()
failure)

>> 
>
>Thanks for testing and reviewing!
>
>Usama

--- Thanks!

2026-11-06.patch_summary: Patch to keep crashkernel CMA pages reserved if activation fails, allowing for easier debugging of kernel crashes.
